reader.title: Armed seizure and expulsion of a Black depot worker in Kansas (1903)
bases: A1 describes one private man seizing a Black stranger at revolver point and marching him to the lockup, followed by a $10 fine and an order to leave town; no mob, assault or killing is reported, so it fits none of the specific types cleanly.
A1, a local item in the Chanute Times, is the only report found in either press.

summary.text: The armed seizure and expulsion of a Black depot worker took place in a Kansas town in late March 1903, when a townsman held an unnamed Black man at revolver point and marched him to the lockup after he was accused of following two women on the street.
The man was held for two days, fined $10 and told to leave town, and he left.
The only known account, a short local item in the Chanute Times, presented the episode as a lighthearted success.
According to the Chanute Times, the man was a stranger in the town who had been working on the construction of a new depot building.
The paper did not name him, the town, the women or his captor.

On "last Saturday night," probably March 21, two women on the street said they noticed they were being followed by "a big negro"; when they quickened their pace he did the same, and they ran until they reached safety.
A man the paper called "a gentleman of nerve" then asked the women to walk back along the same street while he followed at a distance.
When the man reappeared, the gentleman thrust a revolver in his face before he was aware of any trouble and marched him to the lockup.
He was held until Monday night, fined $10 and told to leave the town "and lose no time in doing it," which, the paper said, he did.
The item did not say who imposed the fine or on what charge, and it gave no statement from the man himself.
The Chanute Times ran the story on page 1 of its March 27 issue under the headline "Ordered to Skip, and He Skipped."
Its tone was approving and jocular: the captor was "a gentleman of nerve," the accused was "the darkey" and "the fellow," and the women's account was told as fact.
No other white paper and no Black paper has been found carrying the story.

accounts.label: Local newspaper item
accounts.gist: The ladies were followed and fled; a gentleman used them to draw the man out, seized him with a revolver and jailed him; he was fined and told to leave, and did.

framing.detail: The Chanute Times headed the item 'Ordered to Skip, and He Skipped', called the captor 'a gentleman of nerve' and the man 'the darkey', and gave only the accusers' side.

record_check.dossier: No town named; the item is unlocated local news in a Chanute paper (Independence appears only in the adjacent Methodist conference item on the same page)
No mob or assault described; one armed private man seized him, then a fine and order to leave town (other)
A private 'gentleman of nerve'; officials appear only in the lockup, fine and order to leave
Not taken from custody; he was put into custody by his captor and released after a fine
One unnamed Black man, a stranger working on the new depot building

info: 'Last Saturday night' in a Friday, 1903-03-27 issue, i.e. probably 1903-03-21; detention ran to Monday night (probably 1903-03-23)
Not named; the item ran as unlocated local news on page 1 of the Chanute Times (Chanute, Kan.) and refers only to 'the town' and its 'new depot building'
One unnamed Black man, called 'a big negro' and 'the darkey', a stranger who had been working on the new depot building
Said to have followed two ladies on the street at night, who became frightened and ran
An unnamed 'gentleman of nerve' who had the ladies walk the street again as bait and followed behind

sources.note: Only report, headed 'Ordered to Skip, and He Skipped': a 'big negro' said to have followed two ladies is seized at revolver point by 'a gentleman of nerve', locked up, fined $10 and told to leave town; no town named.
